reason: I'm not running an unsigned .exe from a one-person v0.4 project with no source and no reviews, and IrfanView already flips through my screenshots instantly. The speed numbers are the developer's own, on one PC.
why_switch_or_not: Next/back at 40-50 ms is nice, but IrfanView is already fast enough for PNG screenshots, so I wouldn't gain much. I'd lose my shortcuts and plug-ins (no plug-in system here), and I'd be betting on one developer still maintaining it next year. Video, 3D, a gallery and an editor sound like feature sprawl, and that's more attack surface in something that parses untrusted files.
current_app_pros: Starts instantly, I know every shortcut, and the plug-ins are set up. Batch convert/rename, a quick crop, resize and capture all work, it's tiny, and it has been maintained for decades.
current_app_pains: The UI looks dated, and rapid next/back is a bit slow on very big files. Colour management is fiddly. Nothing that makes me look for a replacement.
objection: One developer, version 0.4: unsigned, no source, no reviews, so will it still be maintained next year, and can I trust it to parse files from my work?
would_change_my_mind: Published source code or a code-signed installer, plus independent reviews or a year or more of regular releases. Also IrfanView-compatible shortcuts, so I don't have to relearn them.
